Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @yaser_arab57

The sixth session of "Sokhan-e Tazeh" was held on Tuesday, 28 Mehr, at the Andishgah of the National Library. At this session, after the recitation of the Holy Quran, our esteemed friends Mr. Keyvan Mehregan, Mousavi Boldeh, Yaser Arab, Salman Sahraei, Dr. Aali, Hojjat al-Islam Golzar, Abdolmotalleb Mohammadkhani, Dr. Morteza Kia, and Kashfi Khansari shared their views and opinions and raised their questions. Then Dr. Hojjatollah Seydi, the respected head of the Securities and Exchange Organization, delivered a speech on the relationship between culture and economy. At this session, the book "Qiyam of Hazrat Fatemeh" was presented to those present on the occasion of the Fatemieh days (peace be upon her), along with the book "University of the Street," authored by Dr. Seydi.☘My questions to Dr. Hojjatollah Seydi 1. We face many social issues and needs in the country whose solution requires the participation of economic resources. Could a mechanism be created to aggregate these needs and social projects within a transparent and evaluable framework, so that companies can participate in solving them in accordance with their capacity and interest? 2. Many companies have a list of their social responsibility measures—from building schools and bridges to supporting cultural and social projects. But why do these measures, even when they have truly been carried out, not necessarily translate into a tangible experience of public good and social trust? Is the issue merely weak information dissemination, or should we reconsider the definition and design of social responsibility? 3. Could a criterion for measuring the social impact of projects also be defined alongside the report of costs and measures carried out—a criterion that shows which problem in people's lives has been solved, to what extent the result is observable and evaluable, and what relationship society has established with these measures?@yaser_arab57

🎥 Rising suicide statistics in 3 groups: doctors, retirees, students. Hamid Pirouei, deputy of the Scientific Population for Suicide Prevention of Iran, said in a roundtable held on this topic at Ensaf News: In war and crisis conditions, suicide statistics usually decrease, and Iran's 1404 statistics also confirm this scientific-empirical finding. He cited reasons such as increased motivation for survival or mental preoccupations as the cause of the decrease in suicide in crisis conditions. Dr. Pirouei said: In the year 404, we witnessed a decrease in suicide in all social groups except three groups: doctors, retirees, and students. This specialist continued: If the statistics had been provided to us in a timely manner, we could have helped the Ministry of Science or Education for intervention. To watch the full video of this meeting, refer to the Ensaf News channel on [Aparat] or [YouTube].
